# Contributing to AI Engineer Interview Field Guide

Thank you for your interest in contributing. This project is a living collection of resources, interview experiences, and practical knowledge for AI Engineers preparing for interviews.


## What We Welcome

Interview experiences. Real stories from AI Engineer interview loops. What companies asked, what the format was, what you wish you had known. These are the most valuable contributions.

Resource suggestions. Tools, frameworks, blog posts, courses, papers, and communities that help AI Engineers prepare for interviews or grow in the role. We favor resources that are practical and current.

Corrections and updates. Broken links, outdated information, tools that have been deprecated, or companies that have changed their interview process.

Webinar notes and summaries. If you attended a relevant talk or workshop, concise notes adapted for AI Engineer interview preparation are welcome.


## How to Contribute

For interview experiences, open an issue using the Interview Experience template. Include the company (or anonymize if you prefer), the role level, the interview format, and what was asked. Specific details help more than general impressions.

For resource suggestions, open an issue using the Resource Suggestion template. Explain why the resource is valuable and which category it belongs in.

For corrections, open a pull request with the fix. Keep the description brief and focused.

For larger contributions (new sections, restructured content), open an issue first to discuss the change before investing time in a pull request.


## Content Guidelines

Write in first person when sharing experiences. "I found that..." is better than "One should consider..."

Be specific and concrete. "The system design round was 45 minutes and focused on designing a RAG pipeline for legal documents" is better than "There was a system design round."

No bold or italic formatting. No horizontal rules. No all-caps for emphasis. Use code ticks for filenames, tool names, and code-related terms like `LangChain` or `vLLM`.

Keep entries concise. One to three sentences for resource descriptions. Longer content belongs in dedicated files.

Focus on AI Engineering, not general software engineering. Resources should be relevant to building AI-powered applications, working with LLMs, or preparing for AI Engineer interviews specifically.


## What We Do Not Accept

Promotional content or affiliate links. Resources should be recommended because they are genuinely useful, not because of a business relationship.

Content behind hard paywalls. Free or partially free resources are preferred. If a paid resource is exceptional, note the cost.

AI-generated interview experiences. We want real stories from real candidates. Fabricated experiences undermine the trust this collection depends on.

Duplicate resources. Check existing entries before suggesting a resource.


## Code of Conduct

Be respectful and constructive. Share knowledge generously. Disagree with ideas, not people. Remember that interview experiences are personal and sometimes stressful: treat contributors with empathy.


## Questions

If you are unsure whether a contribution fits, open an issue and ask. We would rather discuss it than have you invest time on something that does not align with the project.
